input.verdict: Mostly uninformative, with slight support. MEGNet gaps for the PbO polymorphs are spread widely (0.0 to 3.4 eV), and experimental litharge is about 1.9 eV, so the Pb-rich end probably absorbs 2.4 eV photons better than Pb2Sb2O7, which gave low EQE at index 8. Measuring index 0 tests the Pb-rich region, which is far from index 8 on the composition line.

input.verdict: Uninformative to mildly against. The known Sb-rich phases have HSE gaps of 2.7–2.8 eV (Sb2O3, PbSb2O6), which argues against strong absorption at 2.4 eV. The 0.01 eV gap MEGNet gives the best-matching pyrochlore polymorph is not credible. However, the XRD at index 20 includes a strong peak at Q=1.19 that no known phase matches, so the phase there is unidentified. Index 0 is already the Pb-rich endpoint, so I'm using the final merit measurement to explore the untested Sb-rich half.

content.text:
I submitted **index 0** (Pb 0.76 / Sb 0.24) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE of the three I measured, though every value was very low (all under 0.005%).

| Index | Pb fraction | EQE (%) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.76 | **0.0049** | Pb-rich end of the library |
| 8 | 0.52 | 0.0027 | Pb₂Sb₂O₇ composition |
| 20 | 0.17 | 0.0020 | Sb-rich; XRD shows a phase I couldn't match to any known one |

- **Why these three:** Before measuring, I checked the two stable mixed oxides. The models put both on the stability hull. Pb₂Sb₂O₇ has a predicted band gap of about 2.5 eV, close to the 2.4 eV light, so I measured it first. It came out low. The Pb-rich end then did better, which fits the Sb-rich oxides having wider gaps (about 2.7–2.8 eV) and absorbing less of the light.
- **Last measurement:** Index 0 is already the most Pb-rich composition in the library, so there was nothing further to try in that direction. I used the final measurement to test the untested Sb-rich half instead of a near neighbour of index 0. It didn't beat index 0.
- **What's uncertain:** Three measurements across 29 compositions is sparse. The gap between index 0 and the rest is small, and the most promising unmeasured compositions are indices 1–4, next to index 0. I didn't measure any of them, so something there could be better.

All three merit measurements are used; I used 2 of the 5 XRD measurements.
